Latest Update: Meet Some of the Unsung Heroes Who Keep NBC Moving as It Celebrates 100 Years

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1763 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Variety

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, as NBC celebrates its 100th anniversary this year, the manufacturer has been recognizing some of its most memorable stars, TV indicates, producers and even executives.
  • So that’s what Variety is doing here: We found six staffers from throughout NBC who keep the network humming.
  • Dawn DiCicco (Associate Director, “NBC Nightly News”).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, as NBC celebrates its 100th anniversary this year, the manufacturer has been recognizing some of its most memorable stars, TV indicates, producers and even executives. But NBC couldn’t run without some of its unsung heroes — the staffers who do the day-to-day work behind the scenes, usually with very little fanfare.

So that’s what Variety is doing here: We found six staffers from throughout NBC who keep the network humming. These are their stories. Related Stories Brad Pitt Indicates 'Ocean's 14' Not Shooting Until 'Late' 2027 Joshua Jackson Teases ‘Sex, Drugs and Rock 'n' Roll’ in Fresh HBO Max Series ‘How to Survive Without Me’: ‘I'm Getting Too Old For This S---’.

Dawn DiCicco (Associate Director, “NBC Nightly News”).

Dawn DiCicco’s job description as associate director of “NBC Nightly News” wouldn’t exactly fit neatly on a LinkedIn page.

“My job is to know everything about everything all the time. I’m responsible for putting out fires before they start,” she says. “It’s to basically gap fill every sort of gap and keep an eye on everything that goes on air. A lot of my job is anticipating people’s needs and what they’re going to want before they can even think that they’re going to ask for that, so I can already have it ready to go. I’m the final line of defense.”.

Every day is different on “Nightly News.” Depending on how and when news breaks, the show can air up to six times per day. That means moving swiftly and decisively on what news is most worthy of inclusion in the 30-minute telecast. A natural disaster may replace a courtroom trial verdict, a financial free fall in Asia might be inserted into the broadcast and a political brouhaha taken out. It’s a blizzard of news and decision-making.

In a recent development, “For me, those days are the most fun,” she adds. “I love the days where like I walk in here and I have zero idea what’s going to happen. The days where when your whole show gets blown up by, like some kind of crazy verdict or some news breaking. That’s where I thrive best because I like to think if you can work under pressure like that, you can work and do anything.”.

Favorite NBC show of all time: “The Traitors”.

Jeanette Eliot (Senior Director, Events and Special Projects).

According to recent reports, when “Saturday Night Live” was celebrating its 50th anniversary a couple of years ago, lots of people went into action — Lorne Michaels, Adam Sandler … and Jeanette Eliot. Eliot was tasked with ordering 6,000 pairs of Converse sneakers for NBC employees, given as a gift to celebrate the occasion.

Industry observers note that “I got to do that,” Eliot notes. “I wanted to make that happen.”.

In a recent development, eliot, who stared her career as an NBC temp in 1995, has made a lot of things happen over her career. She’s the person who fulfills orders for promotional mailers that go to press, selects items and keepsakes for hundreds of events (including premieres and internal meetings), and finds creative ways to celebrate milestones.

Recent findings suggest that eliot often finds herself starting her day before the sun rises because of the need to deal with retailers from faraway time zones. But she takes enormous pride in getting the work done — no matter the obstacles faced.

Industry observers note that “I’m very hard on myself,” she states. I think my biggest challenge is just not disappointing anybody. I’ll always figure out a way to do it.”.

In a recent development, A recent project included ordering NBC 100 calendars from vendor on the other side of the world. Making things extra tricky: They had to arrive in time so she could send to press by a specific date.

“I didn’t think they were going to make it in time, and when I saw the boxes arrive here from China, it literally brought tears to my eyes,” she indicates.

Favorite NBC show of all time: “American Ninja Warrior”.

Evan Klupt (Senior Director, “Today” Production Operations).

When viewers turn on “Today” each morning, they see a well-lit set, smiling and well-groomed anchors, reporters around the world and a production team that knows the right buttons to push as the two-hour telecast moves along. What they don’t see is Evan Klupt.

Klupt, who has been at NBC since 1995, is among the many “Today” professionals who makes sure the morning program looks like a well-oiled machine. He oversees the show’s production management team that handles everything from setting up live remotes on location, guest logistics and prepping those guests to go on air, among lots of other things.

“My job touches all areas of that production, whether it’s in the studio or on the Plaza in Rockefeller Center,” Klupt claims. “It’s dealing with personnel, hair, makeup, wardrobe, green rooms, concerts and large-scale productions. That’s kind of my beat.”.

It has been revealed that among his NBC highlights are working at 13 Olympics (he met his wife at the 2000 Sydney Games) and traveling the globe. By his count, he’s now worked in 50 countries.

A recent “Today” trip to Ireland put everything into perspective. “We had the show that we did there recently and I was thinking that when viewers tune into something, they only see the anchors,” he notes. “They see a beautiful set with an amazing rainbow going across the set into the skyline of Ireland, but they’re not seeing everything that went into it — procuring the table they’re sitting at, getting the flowers on the desk, shipping hundreds of cases of equipment and dealing with customs, logistics, hotels and transportation. Our group does everything from the very beginning.”.

Favorite NBC show of all time: “Seinfeld”.

Justin Michael Ratchford (Field Producer, “Dateline NBC”).

It has been revealed that if Justin Michael Ratchford hadn’t gone into long-form journalism on “Dateline NBC,” he might have had another career as a therapist. That’s because in his role as an “Dateline NBC” field producer, he often needs to create a comfort zone with those subjects who are about to divulge their lives in front of the camera.

In a recent development, “We have to build those relationships and foster them, to get someone willing to talk,” Ratchford notes. “I typically say, ‘I’m going to ask you about the worst moments of your life.’”.

Recent findings suggest that not only does Ratchford have to develop a feel for how a prospective interviewee will share their story, he also must do it while juggling several areas of production on multiple episodes at once. Putting one story together, or even a bunch of them, is not a linear process.

“A story takes as long as it needs,” Ratchford notes. “We had one story that was started in 2007 and didn’t air until 2021.”.

Recent findings suggest that “Dateline” has also inspired him to explore more avenues in storytelling. “I’m a huge film buff,” he indicates. “That’s what really made me fall in love with this job. Movies and films were my first love. I always said I want to shoot something and see it on a major screen.”.

Favorite NBC show of all time: “The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air”.

Jessica Sheeley-Saunders (Vice President, Productions and Operations, Specials and Live Events).

Recent findings suggest that everyone loves a parade. But maybe not as much as Jessica Sheeley-Saunders. In her job working with specials and live events, Sheeley-Saunders says it’s her job to “connect all the dots between all the departments. It’s a bit like crisis management in solving problems and, a like the mom, making sure everyone’s doing what they’re supposed to be doing.”.

Sheeley-Saunders, who joined NBC three years ago, states she feels honored to be in a position to bring some of the country’s most iconic events — like the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade, the Christmas tree-lighting at Rockefeller Center and this year, the Emmy Awards — and make sure it all goes smoothly.

“In this position, I get to be a part of some of America’s favorite traditions, and it’s just a little surreal,” she notes. “There are 40 million people watching the parade, and I get to be in the front row, making that happen.”.

Calling herself “a proud San Fernando Valley girl, born and raised” and graduate of Cal State Northridge, Sheeley-Saunders indicates she looks forward to being on the streets of New York every year in late November.

According to recent reports, “To stand there on Thanksgiving morning and see the entire city shut down and watch these giant balloons go by … There was a moment when I called my husband and said, ‘I made the right decision. I am so happy that I said yes to this.’”.

Favorite NBC show of all time: “Friends”.

Francine Spray (Senior Vice President, Events and Special Projects, Universal Television Entertainment).

In a recent development, francine Spray joined NBC as a Page in 1988, and has been there for some of its most landmark moments. That’s because she’s the person charged with making sure events go off smoothly, as sheand her team oversee approximately 200 events a year that the company schedules.

Spray is tasked with bringing together premieres, screenings, off-site meetings, press events, receptions, red carpets and more from inception to completion. She knows the best restaurants in Los Angeles to hold an event, the amount of alcohol necessary for a post-Golden Globes soirée and how a post-event party for NBC brass at the Paris Olympics needs to be organized differently than for those Games held in Seoul, Barcelona or Athens.

Spray notes that her job has changed over the years, as the reliance on social media grew in getting promotion and a good word out for the manufacturer’s properties and programming.

Recent findings suggest that “We now need to plan for social and Instagrammable moments,” Spray states. “It’s really a big part of what we do. We have to have a photo moment at every event.”.

According to recent reports, spray and her team had to make a huge pivot during COVID, when people weren’t allowed to gather. She says it was “one of our most transformative times for this department… We had to get hooked on to Zoom in two seconds flat. That was the only way we kept ourselves going from the PR perspective — to do all of those virtual junkets and keep the publicity machine rolling, so to speak.”.

Favorite NBC show of all time: “Hill Street Blues”.

#1055. Should I buy a gaming console just to play GTA 6? That depends on your FOMO.

Should I buy a gaming console just to play GTA 6? That depends on your FOMO.

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1309 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto VI is out now, if you hadn't heard.
  • By that, we mean you might not have a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series console at the ready to play the highly anticipated release.
  • So, let's lay out the cases for and against doing that.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto VI is out now, if you hadn't heard. If you're not playing it but are reading this, we can guess why.

By that, we mean you might not have a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series console at the ready to play the highly anticipated release. If that's the case, you're going to miss out on the biggest gaming launch of the year — and possibly all time. FOMO is a natural human reaction to these sorts of things, and here at Mashable, we fully understand the pain of not being sure whether or not you should buy a console just for GTA 6.

So, let's lay out the cases for and against doing that.

The primary and most obvious reason to buy a console for GTA 6 is that it's the only real way to play it at launch. There is technically another way that we'll cover in a little while, but for all intents and purposes, you cannot have the same experience everyone else is having without buying a PS5 or Xbox Series console.

By all accounts, GTA 6 is a pretty fantastic video game. You probably wouldn't want to miss out on that. What are you going to do while everyone else is having an amazing time parading through Leonida, read books? Come on, that sounds boring.

One thing that's also worth remembering is that other video games exist. A lot of them, in fact. If you buy a PS5 or Xbox Series console, you'll have access to the last six years of current-gen releases, some of which are extremely good. They might even be better than GTA 6! As a fun bonus, through the magic of backward compatibility, ports, remasters, and remakes, you'll also be able to play countless video games from previous generations of hardware, too.

Recent findings suggest that lastly, both consoles (at least the models with disc drives) work as 4K Blu-ray players, if you're into collecting physical versions of movies. That's cool, too.

Recent findings suggest that both consoles have been hard to find in stock (thanks in large part to GTA 6), but the Xbox Series S and PS5 Digital Edition are both in stock at Amazon, as of this writing. If you're not sure whether to buy a PS5 or the Xbox Series X/S, keep scrolling for a breakdown of the pros and cons.

First, foremost, in the biggest, boldest font you can imagine: You shouldn't buy a console just for GTA 6 because they're stupid expensive these days.

It has been revealed that both Xbox and PlayStation have recently increased the prices of their consoles due to real-world economic concerns. The cheapest model right now is a $499 Xbox Series S, and Rockstar hasn't shown us that version of the game yet, leading to speculation that the game is better on PS5, which starts at $599. If you want the best possible version at launch, you'll need a PS5 Pro, which costs $899 — and is currently out of stock at most retailers.

In other words, there just isn't a particularly affordable way to play GTA 6 traditionally at launch, unless you already own the hardware.

There are, of course, other reasons to not get a console for GTA 6. There exists a slim likelihood that you won't like the game, though so far, most people who have played it have come away with positive impressions. It also won't have an online component at launch, and no one knows when it will get one. For a lot of people, GTA Online is the only GTA experience that matters, and that audience will have very little to do in the new game until some nebulous point in the future when Rockstar decides to cater to them.

Maybe you just don't care that much about non-GTA video games, either. If that's the case, it's hard to recommend spending this much money on a box that will only play one game.

There was a lot of anxiety on the internet prior to the game's launch surrounding the potential differences between the different console versions. The good news is that the game is out and has been fully tested by experts, and the verdict is that you almost can't go wrong with GTA 6 on any platform.

Digital Foundry is an outlet and YouTube channel that offers expert-level tech analysis of games, and they have a fairly comprehensive guide to the different console versions of GTA 6. According to DF, both the PS5 and Series X versions run at the same resolution and target the same frame rate, with some performance dips on both in more intense sequences. In other words, the base PS5 and Series X versions are roughly the same, though the PS5's controller does have exclusive haptic feedback features for gameplay like driving cars.

There is also the matter of the PS5 Pro and Xbox Series S consoles, though. DF claims the PS5 Pro is the best version of the game, with a sharper resolution and higher-quality shadows to go along with smoother performance. That was to be expected. Sadly, it sounds like the Series S version is probably the least desirable build of the game. Its visuals have been marginally downgraded with a lower resolution and some reduced visual settings, but more importantly, DF's analysis found that the frame rate can dip below 20fps in extreme circumstances.

Recent findings suggest that we do have good news for Xbox Series S gamers, however. Mashable Editorial Director Eric Miller has played the game on Series S and has had a positive first impression so far. If you have no other way to play GTA 6, it should work, but it will be reduced in quality compared to the others.

There is technically a way to play GTA 6 without buying a new PS5 or Xbox, but it's not a viable alternative for most people.

Recent findings suggest that to be clear, there are multiple massive reasons why you might not want to do this. For starters, it involves a monthly subscription. Beyond that, Microsoft recently imposed strict monthly hour limits on Cloud Gaming. With this system, you will be able to play at most 15 hours of GTA 6 per month. Many people are going to play more than that in the first weekend it's out. Even if those aren't concerns, game streaming is subject to the limits of your home internet, meaning that latency and buffering can and will occur. That version of the game will also be visually downgraded to some degree, per Rockstar.

In a recent development, if game streaming (understandably) doesn't work for you, the last option is to wait for the PC version. Unfortunately, Rockstar has not said anything about when GTA 6 will launch on PC, though a recent report pegged it as coming in early 2027. That will likely be the best version of the game in terms of visuals, but only if you have the requisite hardware. For those who already have capable gaming PCs, this might be the best option for playing GTA 6, provided you're patient enough to wait. For those who don't, this is going to be even more expensive than buying a console, so maybe don't bother.

HBO Max — top pick for premium content.

Disney+ — best for families.

Peacock — low-cost choice for live sport.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • When Women’s Guild Cedars-Sinai reached out to ask Harrison Ford and Calista Flockhart if they would join forces to accept a Hollywood Icon Award at the Stardust Ball, the organization got a quick answer.
  • We said yes, yes, yes,” Flockhart revealed while standing next to her husband on a ballroom stage inside at Beverly Wilshire, A Four Seasons Hotel on Wednesday night.
  • It has been revealed that judging by the look on Ford’s face, it was hard to tell if Flockhart was teasing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Women’s Guild Cedars-Sinai reached out to ask Harrison Ford and Calista Flockhart if they would join forces to accept a Hollywood Icon Award at the Stardust Ball, the organization got a quick answer.

“We didn’t hesitate. We mentioned yes. We said yes, yes, yes,” Flockhart revealed while standing next to her husband on a ballroom stage inside at Beverly Wilshire, A Four Seasons Hotel on Wednesday night. “And I promise you, it was not because we wanted an award. Well, actually maybe [Harrison] did. Between you and me, Harrison complains that he doesn’t get enough attention. But really, it’s true. I’m not joking.” Related Stories Lifestyle Harrison Ford Joins Greg Berlanti, Goldie Hawn and Melissa McCarthy as Paley Gala Honorees Business Byron Allen Sells His Stake in Starz.

It has been revealed that judging by the look on Ford’s face, it was hard to tell if Flockhart was teasing. Either way, they received a loads of attention as the night’s marquee honorees alongside media mogul Byron Allen, who received a humanitarian award for his philanthropic work. Normally a private couple, Ford and Flockhart seemed to enjoy the moment as they beamed with joy and even stopped to share a kiss in front of the capacity crowd. The night’s program also featured host Sheryl Underwood and auctioneer Billy Harris with a performance by Jett Stanfield, Brandon Keith Rogers, A.J. Mendoza and Josh Black of the Firm Men.

Recent findings suggest that also making a massive appearance was Ford’s Star Wars colleague Mark Hamill, who offered a brief tribute to his longtime franchise pal. Attention aside, the night was notable as it marked Ford and Flockhart’s first joint award as a couple. They’ve been in lock step on plenty of red carpets over the course of their decades-long romance but hadn’t shared a stage until Wednesday evening. The Stardust Ball proved to be an ideal situation as they both have ties to and admiration for Cedars-Sinai. But it also offered a chance to pay respects to close friends like physicians Bruce Gewertz and Randy Sherman.

It has been revealed that the former, a nationally known vascular surgeon, served as a technical advisor on Ford’s 1993 thriller The Fugitive, while the latter was an internationally renowned surgeon who helped build plastic surgery programs in Los Angeles while traveling the world treating children with complex deformities. Sherman, who served as vice chair in the surgery department and director plastic surgery at Cedars-Sinai, died July 18, 2023, in an air traffic accident in Santa Fe, Newly introduced Mexico.

Gewertz was in the ballroom and took the stage to offer a tribute. He recalled how he helped The Fugitive’s scribes nail “the medical part of the plot” while training Ford to look as much like a vascular surgeon as possible in the operating room. “I shrewdly negotiated a very rich compensation package with Warner Brothers: Harrison would tuck my kids in at night, and somehow, despite having absolutely no business being in front of a camera, I was included in a small part in the movie, which for the past 33 years has provided me with a steady income every couple of months — after taxes — of about $20,” explained Gewertz.

According to recent reports, beyond spending money, the real reward “the opportunity to get to know Harrison Ford, a man who is “even more impressive than the legendary characters he has created,” Gewertz continued. He then went on to praise Ford’s environmental activism as a long-serving board member of Conservation International and for sticking his neck out on behalf of forests, oceans and fragile ecosystems. Gewertz praised Flockhart’s philanthropic endeavors too as she’s been of service to “causes involving women, children, health and social concerns” through work with For Goodness Sakes, Peace Over Violence and the Violence Intervention Program.

Recent findings suggest that gewertz also revealed that as a couple, they “generously supported” an educational and research fund in honor of Sherman. “Their inspirational philanthropy allows us to pursue discoveries that may change medicines for generations to come, to care for patients who have nowhere else to turn, and most importantly, to honor Randy’s life and legacy,” he said.

In accepting, Ford went first with his comments following a standing ovation. “I’m genuinely touched by what you said,” the actor said to Gewertz, “although I don’t think anyone should hear that many exceedingly kind things about themselves, it feels like a eulogy at my age.”.

The quip landed to plenty of laughs, then Ford turned his attention to Sherman by praising his tireless work on behalf of Operation Smile as he flew all over the world to help “rebuild the faces” of children suffering from cleft palates.

For many years on behalf of Operation Smile, Randy tirelessly traveled the world, rebuilding the faces of children suffering from cleft lips and cleft palates. “When a devastating earthquake hit Haiti in 2010, Randy quickly put together a mission for us in support of Operation Smile. We flew my Cessna Caravan from here to Miami where we picked up a plane load of doctors, technicians, medical equipment and supplies for a remote community in the mountains of Haiti,” recalled Ford. “We landed in the middle of town in a field and walked into a hospital that had two overcome doctors, no usable operating room, no supplies, and many patients in terrible, desperate need. I will never forget watching Randy and the others get to work while I hid my tears at what I was seeing.”.

Industry observers note that ford continued: “Randy flew many such missions over many, many years. I went back to telling stories and making faces for a living. Years later, as soon as he was able, Bruce brought Randy to Cedars-Sinai and put him in charge of plastic surgery. Through his expertise in reconstructive and microsurgery, Randy helped complex patients with previously untreatable birthdays and traumatic physical injuries. Randy Sherman personified the level of care and caring found at Cedars-Sinai.”.

Ford then tossed to Flockhart, who assumed position in front of the microphone to deliver her own remarks. But first, another joke: “It is a rare occasion when I agree with anything that Harrison indicates, but I do. Tonight, I agree. I enthusiastically agree. You should enjoy it [Harrison].”.

It has been revealed that the veteran actress paid her respects to the Women’s Guild, and then closed her remarks by personally thanking the staff at Cedars-Sinai for “the incredible care” that her mother received, and for the way they welcomed Flockhart and her only son into the hospital. “They not only took excellent care of him, they took excellent care of me, the very worried mother,” she added. “I also have a personal experience. The amazing [Dr. David Kulber] fixed my hand. Well, actually he fixed my finger. He fixed my special finger. He fixed the most important finger.”.

With that, Flockhart raised her middle finger in the air. “True story. I was lucky enough to experience the commitment and the humanity firsthand. And that’s a pun, but it was a good one,” she quipped. “OK, so everyone at Cedars-Sinai to me is an icon of brilliant and compassionate care.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Not for the first time, Kevin Parker was anointed the Australian music community’s boss.
  • Kevin Parker’s psychedelic pop outfit was the significant winner, his haul including album of the year for Tame Impala’s fifth studio album, Deadbeat; best solo artist and song of the year for “Dracula.” Tame Impala also won the second annual Global Impact Award presented by Spotify, a category that introduced in 2025 and is designed to sit alongside the ARIA Hall of Fame.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 2026 ARIA Awards are in the books, the empties have been discarded and the hangovers (mostly) settled. With the benefit of hindsight, the Australian recording industry’s 40th annual ceremony at Sydney’s Hordern Pavilion on Wednesday (Nov. 20) was an appropriately large, and noisy, night for such an occasion.

Not for the first time, Kevin Parker was anointed the Australian music community’s boss. And Ecca Vandal deservedly emerged as a hero. For every hero, a villain. Step on up, Artificial Intelligence, the two dirty words on almost every artist’s lips. And for several talents, the night was a real bummer.

Kevin Parker’s psychedelic pop outfit was the significant winner, his haul including album of the year for Tame Impala’s fifth studio album, Deadbeat; best solo artist and song of the year for “Dracula.” Tame Impala also won the second annual Global Impact Award presented by Spotify, a category that introduced in 2025 and is designed to sit alongside the ARIA Hall of Fame.

According to recent reports, this year’s ARIAs didn’t induct any legends into the ARIA Hall of Fame. That was done in June, when six acts entered the special club with a standalone Hall of Fame presentation. One of those inductees, the beloved rock trio Spiderbait, had the honors of closing the 2026 ARIA Awards with a medley of “Calypso,” “Buy Me A Pony” and “Black Betty.”.

According to recent reports, the broadcast opened with a proper surprise — Darren Hayes performing Savage Garden’s “Affirmation,” the title track from the world-conquering Brisbane pop duo’s second and final studio album. With the Olympic Games coming to the Sunshine State in 2032, surely Hayes will be thrown the mic for the Opening Ceremony, the Closing Ceremony, or both.

From Kevin Parker’s big night, to Genesis Owusu’s quiet one, Billboard rounds up the snubs and surprises from the 2026 ARIA Awards.

Sources indicate that kevin Parker winning ARIA Awards, even bunches of them, shouldn’t come as a surprise. What did was the Western Australian production maestro scooping the award for best solo act, for Tame Impala’s fifth studio album Deadbeat. Tame Impala is Kevin Parker — a one-man creation in the studio that grows into a fully-formed band for live performances. Parker won best group, for Tame Impala, in 2013, 2015, and 2020. Until this year, he’d never been nominated for best solo artist. “Hopefully once and for all,” he quipped during his victory speech, “everyone can accept and realize and not need to joke about it that Tame Impala is in fact just one guy.”.

Like Tame Impala, Genesis Owusu had eight nominations for the 2026 ARIA Awards. No artist had more. But unlike Tame Impala, he went home empty handed. It was a strange old night for the Canberra-raised force of nature, who typically cleans-up on awards nights. Just last week, he collected triple j’s J Award for Australian album of the year, for Redstar Wu & The Worldwide Scourge, his third studio album, and doubled-up with the rage Australian music video of the year, winning for the clip to “STAMPEDE,” directed by Isaac Brown. His heaving collection of silverware includes the Australian Music Prize, the Vanda & Young Global Songwriting Competition, AIR Awards, and seven ARIAs. Owusu wasn’t absent from this year’s ARIAs. He got the blood running with a performance of “STAMPEDE,” and on Monday night kicked off ARIA Week with a headline performance of his showcase project Clubstar Wu for Spotify’s ARIA Artist Party.

It’s been a wicked year for Ecca Vandal, in the best possible way. There was her debut performance on U.S. late-night TV; her appearance at Coachella, marking her first-ever spot at a major U.S. festival; a sold-out tour of Australia; and earlier this month, the Australian Music Prize, for her second album Looking for People to Unfollow. Based in Melbourne, Australia, and born in South Africa of Sri Lankan heritage, Ecca Vandal’s fine work wasn’t missed by the ARIAs academy, which awarded her seven nominations. By night’s end, she had four pointy trophies, including the Michael Gudinski breakthrough artist and best independent release. She’ll enjoy that winning feeling for some time yet; Ecca Vandal has been tapped to open for Limp Bizkit on two upcoming international dates next month, in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia (Dec. 9) and Johannesburg, South Africa (Dec. 13). Her performance of “Dance in Debt” and “Cruising to Self Soothe” at the ARIAs kicked ass (watch below).

Industry observers note that there are only so many ARIA Awards to go around (29 categories this year, down from 30). Not everyone will win. Some of the big names who failed to launch included Troye Sivan, Kylie Minogue, Paul Kelly, Keith Urban, and Hilltop Hoods. The Hoods might feel hardest done by, having completed their biggest ever arena tour of Australia, the Never Coming Home Tour, and extended their streak last year with Fall From the Light, their sixth consecutive No. 1 on the ARIA Albums Chart (and seventh in total). Then again, the Hoods, who were recently feted with a own lane in their hometown, Adelaide, don’t stress over such things. Their career collection of ARIA Awards is already in double figures, with 10.

In a recent development, ARIA’s CEO Annabelle Herd doubled down. “For more than a year, everyone in this room has held the line against some of the richest companies on the planet who want to train their AI on your music without asking,” Herd remarked from the stage. “Last month, we polled more than 1,500 Australians and 78% said the companies should have to ask permission before they use Australian creative work. Next week is parliament’s final week of sitting for the year, and before they leave for summer, every MP and senator needs to hear one message from this room. It’s not AIs to take. Every song that you’ve written has taken blood, sweat, and tears. And that’s what AI wants to train on without your permission, and it’s not theirs to take.”.

Tash Sultana, the singer, songwriter and guitarist, used fewer words to get their point across, while presenting the independent category: “roses are red, violets are blue, if you support AI music, f— you.”.

It has been revealed that with their swagger, Britpop spirit, boisterous sing-along choruses, and frontman Tommy O’Dell’s impressive lungs, DMA’S has no shortage of fans. The band has cracked the U.K. in a big way, where three DMA’S albums have entered the top 10, including their latest, self-titled effort, which peaked at No. 9 in September. The LP, the first through a latest deal with Wonderlick and Sony Music, gave the band a long-overdue No.1 on the ARIA Chart, following consecutive podium finishes. The wins piled up at the ARIAs, where DMA’S won a brace, for best group and best rock album, for what was a career night. Previously, the trio owned just one ARIA, for best group in 2023.

#1052. Autistic brains look surprisingly similar on average. Then scientists looked closer.

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (769 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Autistic brains look surprisingly similar on average. Then scientists looked closer.

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (769 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, brain scans have revealed a surprising pattern in people with autism.
  • According to recent reports, the findings, published in JNeurosci, suggest that looking at average brain activity may conceal important differences among people with autism spectrum disorder (ASD).
  • The research was led by Dorit Kliemann and James Traer of the University of Iowa, who worked with collaborators to investigate how brain activity differs between adults with and without autism.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, brain scans have revealed a surprising pattern in people with autism. Although adults with and without autism demonstrated remarkably similar brain activity when researchers compared group averages, a closer examination uncovered striking differences between individuals. These differences were especially pronounced in brain regions involved in understanding and responding to social information.

According to recent reports, the findings, published in JNeurosci, suggest that looking at average brain activity may conceal important differences among people with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). The discovery could help scientists better understand why autism varies so widely from person to person and eventually support more personalized approaches to care.

The research was led by Dorit Kliemann and James Traer of the University of Iowa, who worked with collaborators to investigate how brain activity differs between adults with and without autism.

What Brain Scans Reveal When People Watch Movies.

To explore these differences, the team examined previously collected brain imaging data from Indiana University and Caltech. The recordings captured brain activity as adults with and without autism watched movies from several genres, including animation, action, romantic comedy, and Hitchcockian thrillers.

Movies offered researchers a way to study how the brain responds to a constantly changing stream of sights, sounds, and social interactions. Unlike simple laboratory tasks, movies present a rich mixture of information that more closely resembles the complexity of everyday experiences.

Using the imaging data, the researchers trained a computational model to identify connections between brain activity and different elements of the movies. These included visual details, sounds, and more abstract social information, such as interactions between characters.

After training, the model was able to accurately predict activity across several brain systems.

Kliemann explained why this approach is particularly useful for investigating the social challenges sometimes associated with autism: "The computational model allowed us to look for robust brain responses to many different aspects of the complex, dynamic contexts in the movies.".

A Surprising Difference Hidden by Brain Activity Averages.

The most unexpected finding emerged when researchers compared the two groups.

Industry observers note that at first, the results suggested relatively little difference. When brain responses were averaged across participants, the model predicted activity in various brain systems similarly for adults with and without autism.

However, the picture changed when the researchers examined how much individual participants differed from others in their own group.

According to recent reports, people with autism indicated substantially greater variation in their brain responses than participants without autism. In other words, although the overall group averages looked similar, the responses of individual autistic participants were much less alike.

This increased variability appeared across nearly every brain system examined. The strongest differences occurred in the social brain system, a network of regions involved in processing social information and understanding other people.

Why the Findings Could Change Autism Research.

The results raise important questions about how scientists investigate autism. Many existing approaches to understanding and treating the condition rely heavily on comparing average measurements from groups of autistic and nonautistic individuals.

But if autistic people show considerable differences in how their brains process information, these averages may obscure some of the most meaningful findings.

Traer described the team's surprise: "We were surprised by the similarity of group averages. The results suggest that we need to focus on understanding the details of individual brain responses. How and why do they differ?".

Rather than searching only for brain activity patterns shared by everyone with autism, the findings point toward the potential value of studying individuals and identifying smaller groups with similar characteristics.

Kliemann highlighted what this could mean for future research and support: "Identifying ASD subgroups may help us build a more precise understanding of the condition and help develop ways to provide individually tailored support.".

The researchers now proposal to investigate how these differences in brain activity relate to variations in autism-related behavior. They hope to determine where and when the differences emerge, how they are connected to individual characteristics, and what might explain them.

Ultimately, the findings suggest that understanding autism may require looking beyond the average brain and paying closer attention to the distinctive ways individuals process the world.

#1047. The hidden language of psychopathy is not what scientists expected

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1180 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

The hidden language of psychopathy is not what scientists expected

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1180 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the way people describe their lives may offer surprising clues about their personalities, including traits associated with psychopathy.
  • Sources indicate that researchers examined hundreds of personal life stories and discovered that three major traits associated with psychopathy, boldness, meanness, and disinhibition, were connected to distinctly different ways of using words.
  • The findings, published in the journal Personality and Individual Differences, suggest that psychopathic traits can influence everyday communication in subtle ways that conventional stereotypes often overlook.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the way people describe their lives may offer surprising clues about their personalities, including traits associated with psychopathy. A fresh study from the University of Mississippi challenges the familiar image of psychopaths as cold and emotionless, revealing that their patterns of language can be far more complex than expected.

Sources indicate that researchers examined hundreds of personal life stories and discovered that three major traits associated with psychopathy, boldness, meanness, and disinhibition, were connected to distinctly different ways of using words. Some of the findings were particularly unexpected. For example, people who scored higher in meanness tended to use more positive language, while those with greater boldness used fewer words associated with anxiety.

The findings, published in the journal Personality and Individual Differences, suggest that psychopathic traits can influence everyday communication in subtle ways that conventional stereotypes often overlook.

In a recent development, "The goal here is not to diagnose psychopathy based on language," said Ky Bray, an Ole Miss doctoral candidate in psychology. "It's to point to the fact that psychopathy reveals up in everyday behaviors, even subtle behaviors like language.

"If we want to understand psychopathy and the different traits that comprise it, we need to think creatively about how these traits shape social interaction.".

What 450 Life Stories Revealed About Psychopathy.

The researchers used a psychological framework known as the Triarchic Model of Psychopathy, which examines three distinct personality dimensions. Boldness generally involves confidence and fearlessness, meanness reflects tendencies toward callousness and reduced empathy, and disinhibition involves difficulties with impulse control. According to Laura Drislane, an assistant professor of psychology at the University of Mississippi, these characteristics can affect ordinary behaviors, including how people describe their own experiences.

To investigate these connections, Drislane and Bray recruited 450 participants, including college students and individuals who reported having been incarcerated. Each person responded to open questions about key moments in their life, including their greatest highs, lowest points, and major turning points.

After writing their personal accounts, participants completed a questionnaire designed to measure their levels of psychopathic traits. The researchers then analyzed the written responses using specialized software that identifies patterns in word choice.

The analysis focused on how frequently participants used language associated with different psychological categories, including positive and negative emotions, achievement, social influence or clout, and risk. By comparing these language patterns with the personality scores, the team identified several intriguing relationships.

Surprising Differences in Positive and Negative Language.

Participants with higher disinhibition scores generally used more negative words in their personal stories. They were also less likely to mention friends or use language connected to positive emotions and personal achievement.

Meanness, however, showed a very different pattern. People scoring higher in this trait tended to use more positive language, along with more words related to achievement and rewards. They also used fewer expressions associated with negative emotions.

According to recent reports, boldness was associated with another distinctive pattern. Participants with higher scores used fewer anxiety-related words, including terms such as fear, afraid, and worry. Their personal accounts also contained fewer references to mental illness.

Recent findings suggest that these differences suggest that psychopathic traits do not produce a single recognizable style of communication. Instead, different characteristics are associated with different ways of describing emotions, goals, relationships, and personal experiences.

According to recent reports, "What this tells us is the story we tell about our life has meaning," Drislane said. "It helps people make sense of their experiences, develop a worldview and a coherent sense of who they are.

"What we're starting to see is that in psychopathy, there are traits that relate to differences in meaning-making and the ways people think about their life.".

Why Psychopathy Is More Complex Than the Stereotypes.

The researchers also discovered that the relationship between personality traits and language changed depending on which question participants were answering. Someone describing a difficult experience, for example, might use language differently than when recalling a personal success.

This variation is important because it challenges the assumption that psychopathy is characterized by consistently flat or emotionally empty communication. Instead, the findings indicate that language patterns depend on both the particular psychopathic trait and the context in which someone is telling their story.

"People tend to think of psychopathy as one thing, but it's actually multidimensional," Bray stated. "What we mean when we say that everyone exists on this spectrum. Everyone has some degree of meanness, boldness, and disinhibition.

According to recent reports, "Viewing it from a multidimensional perspective allows us to observe how those traits might manifest in nonforensic populations, in people who have not committed a crime. That allows us to see how these traits affect college students, business professionals, or interpersonal relationships.".

Sources indicate that like many personality conditions, psychopathy is better understood as a spectrum rather than a simple distinction between people who have it and those who do not. At one extreme is the familiar cultural image of a "psychopath," while people at the opposite end score low in all three dimensions.

This approach allows researchers to examine psychopathic traits throughout the general population, including among people who have never committed a crime. It also helps explain why the same broad label can encompass individuals with very different personalities and behaviors.

How Understanding Psychopathic Traits Could Improve Treatment.

Industry observers note that recognizing these differences has implications beyond understanding everyday speech. Researchers have linked dimensions of psychopathy to serious outcomes, including criminal behavior, repeat offending, and intimate partner violence. Examining each trait separately may provide a clearer picture of how these risks develop.

Recent findings suggest that "That's in part why there's a movement away from calling people 'psychopaths,' because we don't view psychopathy as a category," Drislane mentioned. "But psychopathic dimensions can predict important outcomes, things like crime, recidivism, or intimate partner violence.

"What our research, including this paper, suggests is that it's important to look beyond that label and into the different components or dimensions of psychopathy, because each of those dimensions actually has a unique set of outcomes or things that it can predict.".

Researchers also emphasize that psychopathy can be treated, with interventions aimed at reducing problematic symptoms and behaviors. Understanding the psychological processes behind boldness, meanness, and disinhibition could help scientists develop more targeted approaches and potentially identify ways to prevent severe problems from emerging.

Recent findings suggest that "If we want to be able to treat or ideally even prevent psychopathy from developing, we need to understand the mechanisms at play," she stated. "That comes down to understanding the unique contributors for all three of these dimensions.".

What do you remember about the audition process for the show?

I was on another job and we were doing night shoots in Canada, and I got an email about the audition but it was so hectic that I didn’t feel like I could afford to give my attention to anything else. How did you make the decision that you wanted to hold out for the role in War and not the other offer?

It was the character. Johnny’s the audience’s way in. You’re really rooting for him at the beginning, or at least I hope so, and then people are quite disappointed by what he does. But that’s great. It’s complex and divisive. When I was reading the script, I was going, oh God, why’s he done this and that?

Everyone on this show is badly behaved to a degree, but he’s often the person that you feel like could be making better choices….

Recent findings suggest that the other people are smooth-talking, very well put-together, calculated villains. The typical sort. Johnny is not that. He’s done some mad things, the cheating, and he’s a mess. But he’s in a state of constant stress and people do weird stuff when they’re in shock.

Some of what he does feels calculated — but calculated incorrectly — but do you think his affair with Carla was planned or did he get swept up in her beauty and fame?

It has been revealed that the way I saw it at the start was, OK, he’s playing the game. If he gets close to the client, and the client’s able to give him information, that’s great. Obviously he’s attracted to her, and he plays along and flirts, and then he enjoys the flirting. When it’s reciprocated, I think it takes him by surprise and he gets caught up in the moment.

Where do you think the desperation comes from?

I wonder if he would have done any of it had he not got fired. Or had Angus not provoked him at the restaurant at the beginning and made him feel insecure about his job. That ignites a sense of, I’m going to succeed by any means necessary. Being around people that have money and massive careers is very humiliating, and I think that restaurant scene is something of a villain origin story. I know he does punch him, but I imagine everyone thinks, OK, that’s fair.

In the final episode, when he convinces Flora to come take the stand and to read the letter to Carla, is that him being sneaky again to try and win the case to get himself out of a jam? Or is he trying to redeem himself on a deeper level?

Recent findings suggest that I think it was trying to fix the mess he’d made. I think he’s a good person. I know he is. He knows that’s the least he could have done. He lost everything trying to get what he wanted and going about it in the wrong way. He’s got some sneaky skills and this is him putting them to good use. I think he is a good lawyer, and you only get a glimpse of that. His real personality is when he’s working at the restaurant at the beginning of the season. When he’s interviewing at the law firms, it’s a performance he’s putting on and he’s overcompensating for his education and background.

What did they tell you about intends for future seasons of the show?

Recent findings suggest that well they’ve got intends for multiple seasons, and it’s sort of an anthology series following the two law firms over different cases. So I knew there was a possibility for doing more seasons. I don’t want to say much more right now.

Industry News: A mysterious twist in the universe’s oldest light could reveal fresh physics

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1634 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A mysterious twist in the universe's oldest light could offer clues to physics that scientists have yet to discover.
  • Industry observers note that the mystery centers on the cosmic microwave background (CMB), a faint glow of radiation left over from approximately 380,000 years after the Big Bang.
  • When the universe was about 380,000 years old, it had cooled enough to become transparent, allowing light to travel freely through space.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A mysterious twist in the universe's oldest light could offer clues to physics that scientists have yet to discover. But before researchers can determine whether this subtle signal reveals something extraordinary about the cosmos, they must answer a crucial question: Is the effect actually coming from the universe, or could it be an illusion created by the telescopes observing it?

Industry observers note that the mystery centers on the cosmic microwave background (CMB), a faint glow of radiation left over from approximately 380,000 years after the Big Bang. This ancient light provides a remarkable snapshot of the "baby universe" as it existed nearly 13.8 billion years ago, allowing scientists to investigate conditions from the earliest stages of cosmic history.

When the universe was about 380,000 years old, it had cooled enough to become transparent, allowing light to travel freely through space. As radiation scattered off free electrons during this transition, it acquired a small amount of linear polarization. Polarization describes the direction in which light's electric field oscillates, and a similar effect occurs when sunlight scatters through Earth's atmosphere.

Sources indicate that now, observations suggest that the polarization of this ancient radiation may have shifted slightly as the light traveled across the universe. This possible rotation, called cosmic birefringence, is especially intriguing because it could point to physical processes not explained by the Standard Model, the leading theory describing fundamental particles and their interactions. Confirming the effect might even provide latest insights into dark matter and dark energy (see Sidebar).

A Mysterious Cosmic Signal or a Telescope Error?

Recent findings suggest that there is a major obstacle to interpreting this potential discovery. An extremely small error in how a telescope's polarization detectors are aligned can produce a signal that looks almost identical to cosmic birefringence.

Industry observers note that to help address this problem, physicists at the University of California San Diego developed a latest technique for checking how accurately different groups of detectors measure polarization angles. They tested their approach using existing observations collected by the European Space Agency's Planck satellite, which mapped the universe's ancient radiation in extraordinary detail.

It has been revealed that the research was led by Postdoctoral Fellow Anto I. Lonappan, Chancellor's Distinguished Professor of Physics Brian Keating, and Associate Professor of Physics Kam Arnold. Their findings were published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.

Separating Real Cosmic Effects From Instrument Errors.

Previous studies have suggested that the polarization of the CMB may have rotated by just a fraction of a degree over its nearly 14 billion years of travel. Although that sounds insignificant, such a tiny change could have enormous implications for fundamental physics.

In a recent development, unfortunately, a telescope whose polarization detectors are misaligned by a similarly small angle could produce precisely the same apparent rotation. If every detector shares the same alignment error, the resulting measurements cannot distinguish that error from a genuine rotation of the cosmic signal.

According to recent reports, the UC San Diego researchers found a way to investigate the problem from another angle. Rather than relying on a single combined measurement, they compared separate polarization maps generated by different groups of detectors.

If cosmic birefringence is real, its effect should appear consistently across all these maps. By comparing the maps with one another, the researchers can effectively eliminate any rotation shared by all of them. What remains reveals differences in the calibration of the individual detector groups, making it possible to identify inconsistencies that might otherwise complicate the search for latest physics.

"The signal we are looking for is incredibly small, so we have to be certain that we are seeing the universe and not our instrument," stated Lonappan. "Our method gives us a complementary way to check that distinction. Before interpreting a tiny rotation as fresh physics, we want to know that the calibration itself can be trusted.".

Testing the Mystery With Planck Satellite Data.

According to recent reports, to evaluate their technique, the researchers analyzed eight polarization maps produced using Planck observations. They then compared their findings with results from an established approach called the Minami-Komatsu analysis, which is used to distinguish instrumental rotation from possible cosmic birefringence.

According to recent reports, although the two methods rely on different assumptions, they produced consistent results. This agreement provides an important independent check on how relative detector calibration errors are being assessed.

The upcoming approach also has a deliberate limitation. Because it removes any rotation common to all the maps, it cannot independently measure the overall polarization angle or determine how much the universe itself may have rotated the light. Establishing that absolute rotation still requires an independent reference for calibrating the overall angle.

In a recent development, to demonstrate how their findings fit with existing measurements, the researchers combined their reconstruction of relative calibration differences with the common calibration value inferred from the established analysis. This produced an estimated cosmic birefringence angle of 0.37 ± 0.12 degrees, matching the Minami-Komatsu result.

Importantly, this agreement does not independently confirm that the ancient light has actually rotated. Instead, it indicates that the fresh method can reproduce results from the existing framework while providing a separate way to examine potential calibration problems.

Searching for Gravitational Waves From the Early Universe.

The technique could also play an vital role in another major pursuit in cosmology: the search for gravitational waves generated during the universe's earliest moments.

To understand why, scientists distinguish between two patterns of polarization in the cosmic microwave background, known as E modes and B modes.

Sources indicate that E modes were first detected in 2002. They arise from density variations in the early universe and form symmetric polarization patterns. B modes have a different appearance, featuring patterns that resemble curls or swirls.

It has been revealed that one known source of B modes is gravitational lensing, which occurs when the gravity of matter between Earth and the early universe bends and distorts the path of ancient light. Scientists have already observed B modes created through this process.

It has been revealed that however, researchers are also searching for a different kind of B mode that could have been produced by primordial gravitational waves. These ripples in spacetime may have originated during an extremely early period of rapid cosmic expansion, known as inflation. The distinctive B mode signal associated with those primordial gravitational waves has not yet been detected.

Finding it would provide powerful evidence about gravitational waves in the early universe and could offer strong support for particular models of cosmic inflation, potentially transforming scientists' understanding of how the universe began.

Why Extremely Precise Measurements Matter.

The challenge is that even a slight error in a telescope's polarization calibration can cause some of the much stronger E-mode signal to appear incorrectly as B modes. This contamination could make an instrumental artifact look like an exciting cosmological discovery.

Recent findings suggest that the UC San Diego method could help prevent such mistakes by identifying differences in polarization angle calibration among detector groups. That makes it a potentially valuable tool for future experiments searching for the extremely faint signatures of primordial gravitational waves.

This kind of independent verification will become increasingly key as observatories develop the ability to measure cosmic polarization with greater precision. One example is the Simons Observatory, where Keating serves as principal investigator.

As these instruments become more sensitive, researchers will need equally rigorous methods for confirming that the faint signals they detect are genuine features of the universe rather than imperfections in their equipment.

It has been revealed that "The detection of primordial B modes would transform our understanding of the early universe, so the measurement must survive rigorous calibration checks," stated Keating. "Anto has developed a useful new framework for testing relative polarization-angle calibration. This is ultimately about knowing when we can trust a measurement.".

Beyond the Standard Model: Dark Matter and Dark Energy.

The possibility of cosmic birefringence is particularly fascinating because it could reveal physics that lies beyond the Standard Model.

Sources indicate that although this framework has been remarkably successful at describing fundamental particles and their interactions, it cannot explain everything in the universe. Among its most vital unanswered questions are the identity of dark matter and the origin and observed magnitude of dark energy. Together, these mysterious components account for approximately 95% of the universe's total energy density.

It has been revealed that one possible explanation for cosmic birefringence involves a hypothetical field associated with particles resembling axions. Such a field could interact with light and gradually alter its polarization as it crosses the universe. However, these particles have not been confirmed to exist, and they would not necessarily be responsible for dark matter.

Other theoretical explanations connect the possible rotation to fields associated with dark energy, the mysterious phenomenon linked to the accelerating expansion of the universe.

If cosmic birefringence is eventually confirmed, it could provide an entirely new way to investigate these cosmic mysteries and reveal evidence of physical laws beyond those at the moment understood.

In a recent development, for now, the first challenge is ensuring that the subtle signal can be trusted. By giving researchers another way to identify potential measurement errors, the latest technique strengthens the foundation for future discoveries that could reshape our picture of the universe.

#1041. Hundreds of millions at risk from Chinese shopping app malware

📅 02 Apr 2023 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1936 w)

Hundreds of millions at risk from Chinese shopping app malware

📅 02 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1936 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNN

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It is one of China’s most popular shopping apps, selling clothing, groceries and just about everything else under the sun to more than 750 million people a month.
  • But according to cybersecurity researchers, it can also bypass people’ cell phone security to monitor activities on other apps, check notifications, read private messages and change settings.
  • While many apps collect vast troves of user data, sometimes without explicit consent, experts say e-commerce giant Pinduoduo has taken violations of privacy and data security to the next level.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It is one of China’s most popular shopping apps, selling clothing, groceries and just about everything else under the sun to more than 750 million people a month.

But according to cybersecurity researchers, it can also bypass people’ cell phone security to monitor activities on other apps, check notifications, read private messages and change settings.

And once installed, it’s tough to remove.

While many apps collect vast troves of user data, sometimes without explicit consent, experts say e-commerce giant Pinduoduo has taken violations of privacy and data security to the next level.

In a detailed investigation, CNN spoke to half a dozen cybersecurity teams from Asia, Europe and the United States — as well as multiple former and current Pinduoduo employees — after receiving a tipoff.

In a recent development, multiple experts identified the presence of malware on the Pinduoduo app that exploited vulnerabilities in Android operating systems. Organization insiders said the exploits were utilized to spy on people and competitors, allegedly to boost sales.

“We haven’t seen a mainstream app like this trying to escalate their privileges to gain access to things that they’re not supposed to gain access to,” said Mikko Hyppönen, chief research officer at WithSecure, a Finnish cybersecurity firm.

“This is highly unusual, and it is pretty damning for Pinduoduo.”.

Malware, short for malicious software, refers to any software developed to steal data or interfere with computer systems and mobile devices.

Evidence of sophisticated malware in the Pinduoduo app comes amid intense scrutiny of Chinese-developed apps like TikTok over concerns about data security.

Some American lawmakers are pushing for a national ban on the popular short-video app, whose CEO Shou Chew was grilled by Congress for five hours last week about its relations with the Chinese government.

In a recent development, the revelations are also likely to draw more attention to Pinduoduo’s international sister app, Temu, which is topping US download charts and fast expanding in other Western markets. Both are owned by Nasdaq-listed PDD, a multinational firm with roots in China.

While Temu has not been implicated, Pinduoduo’s alleged actions risk casting a shadow over its sister app’s global expansion.

There is no evidence that Pinduoduo has handed data to the Chinese government. But as Beijing enjoys significant leverage over businesses under its jurisdiction, there are concerns from US lawmakers that any company operating in China could be forced to cooperate with a broad range of security activities.

The findings follow Google’s suspension of Pinduoduo from its Play Store in March, citing malware identified in versions of the app.

An ensuing report from Bloomberg said a Russian cybersecurity firm had also identified potential malware in the app.

Pinduoduo has previously rejected “the speculation and accusation that Pinduoduo app is malicious.”.

CNN has contacted PDD multiple times over email and phone for comment, but has not received a response.

Pinduoduo, which boasts a user base that accounts for three quarters of China’s online population and a market value three times that of eBay (EBAY), wasn’t always an online shopping behemoth.

Founded in 2015 in Shanghai by Colin Huang, a former Google employee, the startup was fighting to establish itself in a market long dominated by e-commerce stalwarts Alibaba (BABA) and JD.com (JD).

It succeeded by offering steep discounts on friends-and-family group buying orders and focusing on lower-income rural areas.

According to recent reports, pinduoduo posted triple digit growth in monthly consumers until the end of 2018, the year it listed in New York. By the middle of 2020, though, the increase in monthly users had slowed to around 50% and would continue to decline, according to its earnings reports.

It was in 2020, according to a current Pinduoduo employee, that the organization set up a team of about 100 engineers and product managers to dig for vulnerabilities in Android phones, develop ways to exploit them — and turn that into profit.

According to the source, who requested anonymity for fear of reprisals, the tech giant only targeted users in rural areas and smaller towns initially, while avoiding users in megacities such as Beijing and Shanghai.

“The goal was to reduce the risk of being exposed,” they mentioned.

By collecting expansive data on user activities, the organization was able to create a comprehensive portrait of people’ habits, interests and preferences, according to the source.

This allowed it to improve its machine learning model to offer more personalized push notifications and ads, attracting users to open the app and place orders, they said.

The team was disbanded in early March, the source added, after questions about their activities came to light.

PDD didn’t reply to CNN’s repeated requests for comment on the team.

Approached by CNN, researchers from Tel Aviv-based cyber firm Check Point Research, Delaware-based app security startup Oversecured and Hyppönen’s WithSecure conducted independent analysis of the 6.49.0 version of the app, released on Chinese app stores in late February.

Recent findings suggest that google Play is not available in China, and Android users in the country download their apps from local stores. In March, when Google suspended Pinduoduo, it mentioned it had found malware in off-Play versions of the app.

The researchers found code designed to achieve “privilege escalation”: a type of cyberattack that exploits a vulnerable operating system to gain a higher level of access to data than it’s supposed to have, according to experts.

“Our team has reverse engineered that code and we can confirm that it tries to escalate rights, tries to gain access to things normal apps wouldn’t be able to do on Android phones,” remarked Hyppönen.

Industry observers note that the app was able to continue running in the background and prevent itself from being uninstalled, which allowed it to boost its monthly active user rates, Hyppönen said. It also had the ability to spy on competitors by tracking activity on other shopping apps and getting information from them, he added.

Check Point Research additionally identified ways in which the app was able to evade scrutiny.

The app deployed a method that allowed it to push updates without an app store review process meant to detect malicious applications, the researchers remarked.

They also identified in some plug-ins the intent to obscure potentially malicious components by hiding them under legitimate file names, such as Google’s.

“Such a technique is widely used by malware developers that inject malicious code into applications that have legitimate functionality,” they remarked.

Industry observers note that in China, about three quarters of smartphone users are on the Android system. Apple (AAPL)’s iPhone has 25% market share, according to Daniel Ives of Wedbush Securities.

Sergey Toshin, the founder of Oversecured, said Pinduoduo’s malware specifically targeted different Android-based operating systems, including those used by Samsung, Huawei, Xiaomi and Oppo.

CNN has reached out to these companies for comment.

Toshin described Pinduoduo as “the most dangerous malware” ever found among mainstream apps.

“I’ve never seen anything like this before. It’s like, super expansive,” he said.

Most phone manufacturers globally customize the core Android software, the Android Open Source Project (AOSP), to add unique features and applications to their own devices.

Toshin found Pinduoduo to have exploited about 50 Android system vulnerabilities. Most of the exploits were tailor made for customized parts known as the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) code, which tends to be audited less often than AOSP and is therefore more prone to vulnerabilities, he remarked.

According to recent reports, pinduoduo also exploited a number of AOSP vulnerabilities, including one which was flagged by Toshin to Google in February 2022. Google fixed the bug this March, he noted.

According to Toshin, the exploits allowed Pinduoduo access to users’ locations, contacts, calendars, notifications and photo albums without their consent. They were also able to change system settings and access users’ social network accounts and chats, he remarked.

Industry observers note that of the six teams CNN spoke to for this story, three did not conduct full examinations. But their primary reviews revealed that Pinduoduo asked for a large number of permissions beyond the normal functions of a shopping app.

They included “potentially invasive permissions” such as “set wallpaper” and “download without notification,” remarked René Mayrhofer, head of the Institute of Networks and Security at the Johannes Kepler University Linz in Austria.

Industry observers note that suspicions about malware in Pinduoduo’s app were first raised in late February in a report by a Chinese cybersecurity firm called Dark Navy. Even though the analysis didn’t directly name the shopping giant, the report spread swiftly among other researchers, who did name the tech giant. Some of the analysts followed up with their own reports confirming the original findings.

Soon after, on March 5, Pinduoduo issued a new enhancement of its app, version 6.50.0, which removed the exploits, according to two experts who CNN spoke to.

Two days after the patch, Pinduoduo disbanded the team of engineers and product managers who had developed the exploits, according to the Pinduoduo source.

It has been revealed that the next day, team members found themselves locked out of Pinduoduo’s bespoke workplace communication app, Knock, and lost access to files on the manufacturer’s internal network. Engineers also found their access to substantial data, data sheets and the log system revoked, the source said.

Sources indicate that most of the team were transferred to work at Temu. They were assigned to different departments at the subsidiary, with some working on marketing or developing push notifications, according to the source.

A core group of about 20 cybersecurity engineers who specialize in finding and exploiting vulnerabilities remain at Pinduoduo, they stated.

Toshin of Oversecured, who looked into the upgrade, said although the exploits were removed, the underlying code was still there and could be reactivated to carry out attacks.

Pinduoduo has been able to grow its user base against a backdrop of the Chinese government’s regulatory clampdown on Major Tech that began in late 2020.

That year, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology released a sweeping crackdown on apps that illegally collect and use personal data.

In 2021, Beijing passed its first comprehensive data privacy legislation.

The Personal Information Protection Law stipulates that no party should illegally collect, process or transmit personal information. They’re also banned from exploiting internet-related security vulnerabilities or engaging in actions that endanger cybersecurity.

Pinduoduo’s apparent malware would be a violation of those laws, tech policy experts say, and should have been detected by the regulator.

Sources indicate that “This would be embarrassing for the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, because this is their job,” said Kendra Schaefer, a tech policy expert at Trivium China, a consultancy. “They’re supposed to check Pinduoduo, and the fact that they didn’t find (anything) is embarrassing for the regulator.”.

The ministry has regularly published lists to name and shame apps found to have undermined user privacy or other rights. It also publishes a separate list of apps that are removed from app stores for failing to comply with regulations.

Pinduoduo did not appear on any of the lists.

CNN has reached out to the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and the Cyberspace Administration of China for comment.

On Chinese social media, some cybersecurity experts questioned why regulators haven’t taken any action.

In a recent development, “Probably none of our regulators can understand coding and programming, nor do they understand technology. You can’t even understand the malicious code when it’s shoved right in front of your face,” a cybersecurity expert with 1.8 million followers wrote last week in a viral post on Weibo, a Twitter-like platform.

The post was censored the next day.

CNN’s Kristie Lu Stout and Sean Lyngaas contributed reporting.
